description.en: Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
description.fr: Utiliser a devant un son consonne et an devant un son voyelle.

explanation.en: English has no grammatical gender: the choice between a and an depends only on the FIRST SOUND of the next word. Before a consonant sound, use a: a book, a train. Before a vowel sound, use an: an apple, an airport. It's the sound that counts, not the letter: a university (you-), an hour (silent h).
explanation.fr: L'anglais n'a pas de genre grammatical : le choix entre a et an dépend uniquement du PREMIER SON du mot suivant. Devant un son consonne, utilise a : a book, a train. Devant un son voyelle, utilise an : an apple, an airport. C'est le son qui compte, pas la lettre : a university (son "you"), an hour (h muet).

title.en: The present simple and the third-person -s
title.fr: Le présent simple et le -s de la 3e personne

description.en: The verb keeps its base form, except he/she/it which adds -s (-es, -ies).
description.fr: Le verbe garde sa forme de base, sauf he/she/it qui ajoute -s (-es, -ies).

explanation.en: In the present simple, the verb is the bare form for I/you/we/they: I work, you eat. Only the third person singular (he/she/it) changes, adding -s: he works. Spelling: verbs in -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o add -es (he goes, she watches); verbs in consonant + y change to -ies (he studies). The verb be is fully irregular: I am, you are, he is.
explanation.fr: Au présent simple, le verbe garde sa forme de base pour I/you/we/they : I work, you eat. Seule la troisième personne du singulier (he/she/it) change, en ajoutant -s : he works. Orthographe : les verbes en -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o ajoutent -es (he goes, she watches) ; les verbes en consonne + y passent à -ies (he studies). Le verbe be est complètement irrégulier : I am, you are, he is.

description.en: Negate with don't (doesn't for he/she/it) + the base verb.
description.fr: Nier avec don't (doesn't pour he/she/it) + la base verbale.

explanation.en: The present simple negates with the auxiliary do: don't (do not) + base verb: I work → I don't work. For he/she/it, use doesn't — and the main verb LOSES its -s, because doesn't already carries it: she works → she doesn't work. The verb be negates directly, without do: I'm not, he isn't.
explanation.fr: Le présent simple se nie avec l'auxiliaire do : don't (do not) + base verbale : I work → I don't work. Pour he/she/it, utilise doesn't — et le verbe principal PERD son -s, car doesn't le porte déjà : she works → she doesn't work. Le verbe be se nie directement, sans do : I'm not, he isn't.

translations.fr: Je ne bois pas de café.

description.en: Add -s; -es after s/sh/ch/x/o; -ies after consonant + y; some nouns are irregular or uncountable.
description.fr: Ajouter -s ; -es après s/sh/ch/x/o ; -ies après consonne + y ; certains noms sont irréguliers ou indénombrables.

explanation.en: Most nouns add -s: book → books. Nouns in -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o add -es: bus → buses. Consonant + y becomes -ies: city → cities. Some plurals are irregular: person → people. And uncountable nouns (water, milk, bread, rice…) normally have no plural at all — they stay the same.
explanation.fr: La plupart des noms ajoutent -s : book → books. Les noms en -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o ajoutent -es : bus → buses. Consonne + y devient -ies : city → cities. Certains pluriels sont irréguliers : person → people. Et les indénombrables (water, milk, bread, rice…) n'ont normalement pas de pluriel — ils restent identiques.
